title: as (as I walked ... / as I was ... etc.)
subtitle: as she drove away / as I was hungry
summary: Use as to say that two things happen at the same time, or to mean 'because', and know when to use when instead.

lesson.heading: as = at the same time as
lesson.text: You can use **as** when two things happen together at the same time. You can also say that something happened **as** you were doing something else (in the middle of doing it).

examples.text: We all waved goodbye to Liz **as** she drove away.
examples.note: we waved and she drove away at the same time

examples.text: **As** I walked along the street, I looked in the shop windows.
Can you turn off the light **as** you go out, please?
Kate slipped **as** she was getting off the bus.
We met Paul **as** we were leaving the hotel.

lesson.heading: just as, and longer periods
lesson.text: You can also use **just as** (= exactly at that moment). We also use **as** when two things happen together over a longer period of time - one develops while the other develops.

examples.text: **Just as** I sat down, the doorbell rang.
I had to leave **just as** the conversation was getting interesting.
**As** the day went on, the weather got worse.
I began to enjoy the job more **as** I got used to it.

lesson.heading: as or when? (time)

left.label: as - two things happen at the same time
examples: **As** I drove home, I listened to music. (= at the same time)

right.label: when - one thing happens after another
examples: **When** I got home, I had something to eat. (not as I got home)

lesson.note: We use as only if two things happen at the same time. Use when (not as) if one thing happens after another.

lesson.heading: as = because
lesson.text: **As** also means 'because'. You can also use **since** in this way.

examples.text: **As** I was hungry, I decided to find somewhere to eat.
**As** it's late and we're tired, let's get a taxi home.
We watched TV all evening **as** we didn't have anything better to do.
**As** I don't watch TV any more, I gave my television to a friend of mine.
**Since** it's late and we're tired, let's get a taxi home.

left.label: as = because
examples: David wasn't in the office **as** he was on holiday. (= because he was on holiday)
**As** they lived near us, we used to see them quite often. (= because they lived near us)

right.label: when = at the time that
examples: David lost his passport **when** he was on holiday. (= during the time he was away)
**When** they lived near us, we used to see them quite often. (= at the time they lived near us)

lesson.text: If you can replace as with 'while' the meaning is 'at the same time'; if you can replace it with 'because', it gives a reason. If neither works, you probably need when.

exercises.prompt: 'As I was hungry, I decided to find somewhere to eat.' What does as mean here?
exercises.explanation: Here as gives the reason: because I was hungry.

exercises.prompt: In these sentences as means 'at the same time as'. Match the two halves.

pairs.left: We all waved goodbye to Liz

pairs.right: as she told me her story.
as I was taking a hot dish out of the oven.
as the two teams came onto the field.

pairs.left: A dog ran out in front of the car
pairs.right: as we were driving along the road.

exercises.prompt: Today is a public holiday, so all government offices are shut. Say this with as (= because).
exercises.answer: As today is a public holiday, all government offices are shut.
exercises.explanation: As (= because) + the reason, then the result.

exercises.prompt: I can't go to the concert, so you can have my ticket. Say this with as (= because).
exercises.answer: As I can't go to the concert, you can have my ticket.
exercises.explanation: As I can't go = because I can't go.

exercises.prompt: What does as mean in each sentence?

items.text: As they lived near us, we used to see them quite often.
Kate slipped as she was getting off the bus.
As I was tired, I went to bed early.
Unfortunately, as I was parking the car, I hit the car behind me.
As we climbed the hill, we got more and more tired.
We decided to go out to eat as we had no food at home.
As we don't use the car very often, we've decided to sell it.

exercises.statement: As the day went on, the weather got worse.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Two things developed together over a longer period, so as is right.

exercises.statement: Julia got married as she was 22.
exercises.explanation: Julia got married when she was 22. Being 22 is a point in time, not something happening at the same time or a reason.

exercises.statement: He dropped the glass as he was taking it out of the cupboard.
exercises.explanation: Correct. It happened while he was in the middle of doing something else.

exercises.statement: I used to live near the sea as I was a child.
exercises.explanation: I used to live near the sea when I was a child. Here we mean 'at the time that', not 'because' or 'at the same moment'.

exercises.prompt: David lost his passport ___ he was on holiday.
exercises.explanation: We mean 'during the time he was away', so when. As would mean 'because', which makes no sense here.

exercises.prompt: We watched TV all evening ___ we didn't have anything better to do.
exercises.explanation: As (or since) = because: we watched TV because we had nothing better to do.

options: When I left school, I didn't know what to do.
As I left school, I didn't know what to do.
Just as I left school, I didn't know what to do.
exercises.explanation: Leaving school is a point in time after which something else was true, so when (not as) is correct.
